# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): image blocks OUTSIDE the kept region —
  first seen before the LAST renumbering boundary — evict to
  `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders (payload-only, JSONL
  byte-identical); kept-region images ride on under the normal caps; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
  (`isPayloadTooLargeError`), surface wording in `image_drop_ux.dart`
  (`ImageDropReason.evicted`).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape (no eviction, no ladder). `agent_loop.dart` applies it in
  `_buildRequestContext` after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing
  repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family

# Auto-compaction and the trigger tuning

Auto-compaction keeps a long session inside the model's context window by
folding older history into a structured checkpoint summary. This page is
about WHEN it fires — the trigger — and the `compaction:` config keys
that let you move it (gh-2098).

## The trigger model

The trigger evaluates TWO channels at every turn boundary and fires when
either crosses (gh-1742):

- **Estimate channel** — the chars/4 request estimate of the live
  transcript.
- **Observed channel** — the provider-reported accepted context of the
  last completed request (`usage.input + usage.cacheRead`). Observed
  wins: the pressure is `max(estimate, observed)`, and an
  observed-only crossing runs the pass FORCED (the estimate cannot see
  it).

Both channels compare against the same line: `window − reserveTokens`,
where the reserve comes from `CompactionSettings.forWindow(window)` —
the gh-1742 curve:

- `reserve = min(65536, max(window ~/ 16, legacy flat curve))` — 6.25%
  of the window on the proportional band (≥ 262,144), floored by the
  legacy flat 16Ki curve below it. Above 262k the trigger sits at
  **93.75% of the window**; on a 128k window the flat 16Ki reserve puts
  it at 87.2%.
- `keepRecentTokens = min(131072, max(window ~/ 8, legacy curve))` —
  where the context restarts after a pass.

## The tuning keys (gh-2098)

In `~/.fah/config.yaml` (user scope) or `<project>/.fah/config.yaml`
(project scope, wins per key):

```yaml
compaction:
  # Fire when the anchored context reaches 75% of the window.
  triggerRatio: 0.75
  # OR set the headroom directly (mutually exclusive with triggerRatio):
  # reserveTokens: 50000
  # And/or override where the context restarts after a pass:
  # keepRecentTokens: 80000
```

- `triggerRatio` (0 < r < 1): the trigger line moves to `r × window`.
  Implemented as `reserve = window − floor(r × window)` — one reserve
  value, so EVERY window-derived consumer moves together: both trigger
  channels, the structured engine's gate and fragile-band escalation,
  the ctx meter, the spill budget, and subagent children (the CLI
  passes the merged section to the task executor).
- `reserveTokens` (positive int): the headroom set directly — the
  forWindow curve's reserve is replaced. `triggerRatio` and
  `reserveTokens` are two spellings of the same knob (the trigger
  line); configuring both is a boot error.
- `keepRecentTokens` (positive int): the post-compaction kept-recent
  region replaces the forWindow curve's.

**Absent keys → byte-identical gh-1742 behavior.** The tuning applies
over the scaled forWindow curve, not instead of it: a ratio overrides
only the trigger line, only a configured `keepRecentTokens` overrides
the keep curve.

Validation is strict (the whole `compaction:` section has been since
issue #148): a mistyped value, a ratio at/below 0 or at/above 1, a
non-positive budget, or the ratio+reserve combination throws a named
`ConfigException` at boot and at `fa config set` — nothing is persisted
that the next boot would reject.

Degenerate-guard note (mirrored from the forWindow curve): a reserve
over half the window (a ratio below ~0.5) clamps to `window ~/ 4`, and
a keep over the window clamps to `window ~/ 2` — a pass must always
free tokens.

Precedence for a run:

1. an explicit full `CompactionSettings` pin (hosts only — no yaml
   surface), with the tuning composed over it;
2. a non-empty `compaction:` tuning — a user pin;
3. the bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) over the forWindow
   curve — it retunes the DEFAULTS for a bench run and never rewrites a
   pinned section (gh-1604).

The Flutter app host does not read the tuning keys yet (it reads only
`compaction.engine` today — the same surface `judgeBudgetSeconds` had
before gh-2098); its wiring stays byte-identically on the forWindow
curve.

## Default decision and the benchmark note

**The legacy curve stays the default.** Absent keys are
byte-identical by contract; moving every session to the 0.75–0.80 band
silently multiplies compaction frequency (each pass is an LLM call on
the summarizer role — cost and latency), and the published Context Rot
curve degrades gracefully, not cliff-edge: the industry band buys
quality on very long sessions, at a measurable frequency price
everywhere. Operators of large-window classes opt in per scope; 0.80
is the informed middle (fires at 80% with a modest frequency increase).

Method (reproduce with your own recorded session — the curve is a
private artifact, the sim is standalone):

```bash
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <session.jsonl> \
  --window 128000 --window 200000 --window 400000
# deltas scaled ×3 = an emulated marathon riding the same per-request
# growth shape:
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <session.jsonl> --scale 3 \
  --window 200000 --window 400000
```

The sim replays the recorded per-request observed contexts
(`input + cacheRead`) as a sawtooth: on crossing the policy's line the
context restarts at the keep curve and continues riding the recorded
growth deltas.

Recorded session (218 requests, observed context 19,828 → 178,771;
the gh-1742 anchor channel):

| window | policy | trigger | first fire | fires over the curve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128k | legacy (0.9375) | 87.20% | 87.48% | 1 |
| 128k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 80.21% | 1 |
| 128k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 75.08% | 2 |
| 200k | legacy (0.9375) | 91.81% | never | 0 |
| 200k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 80.01% | 1 |
| 200k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 75.38% | 1 |
| 400k | legacy (0.9375) | 93.75% | never | 0 |
| 400k | 0.80 | 80.00% | never | 0 |
| 400k | 0.75 | 75.00% | never | 0 |

The same curve with per-request deltas scaled ×3 (an emulated
large-window marathon):

| window | policy | trigger | first fire | fires over the curve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200k | legacy (0.9375) | 91.81% | 92.30% | 2 |
| 200k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 84.45% | 3 |
| 200k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 77.11% | 3 |
| 400k | legacy (0.9375) | 93.75% | 93.83% | 1 |
| 400k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 80.25% | 1 |
| 400k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 76.43% | 1 |

Reading: on the recorded session the legacy default never fires at
200k/400k — the session completes inside the window, exactly the
late-fire profile the ticket names; 0.80 fires once at 80% with no
extra passes; 0.75 buys 5 more points of headroom for a doubled pass
count on the 128k class. On the ×3 marathon the frequency cost is
+50% (2 → 3 passes at 200k), not an order of magnitude — the informed
opt-in price.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- feat(gh-2098): the auto-compact trigger is user-configurable —
  `compaction.triggerRatio` / `compaction.reserveTokens` /
  `compaction.keepRecentTokens` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (per-key deepest scope wins) override the gh-1742
  `forWindow` curves; absent keys stay byte-identical (golden-pinned).
  `triggerRatio` (0 < r < 1) pins the trigger line at r × window
  (reserve = window − floor(r·window)) so every window-derived consumer
  moves together — both trigger channels (estimate + the gh-1742
  observed anchor), the structured engine's gate and fragile-band
  escalation, the ctx meter, the spill budget, and task children (the
  CLI threads the merged section through the executor). `reserveTokens`
  sets the headroom directly (mutually exclusive with `triggerRatio` —
  strict named `ConfigException`s, also enforced at `fa config set` —
  nothing persists that the next boot would reject); `keepRecentTokens`
  overrides the post-pass kept region. Degenerate guards mirror
  forWindow (reserve > window/2 clamps to window/4, keep > window
  clamps to window/2) so a pass always frees tokens. A non-empty tuning
  is a user pin: the bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`)
  never rewrites it (gh-1604's rule). Default decision documented in
  `docs/compaction.md` with the benchmark note
  (`bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart`, fire points + frequency at
  0.9375 vs 0.80 vs 0.75 on a recorded 218-request session): the legacy
  curve stays the default (byte-identical contract + pass-frequency
  cost), 0.80 is the informed opt-in. Stale doc comment fixed: the CLI
  settings field described a ratio-based default
  ("ratio 0.7, reserve 50000, keep 80000") that never shipped — the
  field now says what it does and points at [compactionTuning].
- fix(gh-2097): auto-compact measures honestly — no more stale pre-run
  estimates or «0 freed» basis flips. (1) `StructuredCompactor.run()`
  re-anchors the agent state from the session projection BEFORE any
  trigger/before/over math: the in-memory transcript can lag the session
  file (an in-memory tail cut, a second writer appending to the same
  session between runs), and the stale basis computed `over` ≈ 1.4k
  where ~177k was needed — the deterministic hide under-sized every
  pass and the run paid extra passes/minutes; one projection build
  bounded by the ledger cache (O(changed records)) now starts every
  run. (2) Pass reports render an upward basis jump explicitly:
  `StructuredCompactionPass`/`AutoCompactorPass` gain `basisReadTokens`
  (a pass appends only shrinkers, so an after-count above its
  before-count is a second writer's records entering the projection,
  never a regression) and `formatCompactionReport` prints
  `basis re-read: +Nk` instead of a clamped `0 freed · 0%`; the small
  restamp jitter (no flip metadata) keeps its `0 freed` clamp. (3) The
  compaction hooks' diagnostic lines (`auto-compact pass/retry/done`)
  now carry `sid=` like every other compaction lifecycle line, and the
  diagnostic appends run through one serialized in-order chain
  (`flushDiagnosticLog()`, awaited by the REPL teardown and the
  headless finally) — bursts land complete instead of being dropped by
  unawaited fire-and-forget appends racing the process exit. AC: a
  two-writer fixture asserts correct first-pass sizing; golden tests

`buildContextMessages` handles structured projection (renderStructuredMessages). All machinery confirmed. Now — session survival directive: "every write this card adds is append-only/additive; no migration rewrites or replaces session files; a fixture proves an old (large) session loads unchanged — byte-identical apart from the new additive records."

My emergency tier writes ONLY `appendHiddenRange` (additive records). The trim valve is in-memory only. So the session JSONL grows only by `hidden_range` records. The fixture test: build a session file, run relief, verify the file's prefix bytes are unchanged and only appended records differ. 

Also the post-turn mode doesn't write anything new to the session itself.

Now — one more thing to check: the `_relieveOverWindow` in the CLI has this invariant: "The loop re-measures the returned list on the same basis ([_liveRequestTokens]), so a list that is still over the window is refused there too (E1 fail-fast, never a loop)". So relief returns null when nothing shrunk. Keep that.

Also `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — session fixture patterns. And check `test/compaction/compaction_session_test.dart` for how a Session is built in tests (JsonlSessionRepo on a temp file).

content.text:
# gh-2099: [GOAL] compaction: two-tier engine — deterministic emergency relief (mid-turn, seconds) + quality tier at turn boundary (post-turn/async)

## Description

## Problem

Compaction runs on the critical path, and the mid-turn over-window relief (`overWindowRelief`) invokes a **full** auto-compact run — judge first. With a slow or unusable judge model class this turns an in-turn context overflow into a long silent stall (the relief is a declared "long silent window": structured ≤15 min + classic ≤15 min). Industry practice keeps emergency relief deterministic and moves routine consolidation off the critical path (post-turn / background).

## Proposed change

Split the engine into two tiers:

1. **Emergency tier** (mid-turn; deterministic; seconds; no LM): hide the biggest/stalest tool-result records (keep-N-recent per tool class), dedup repeated reads of the same path, local trim valve. The over-window relief and message-cap relief call ONLY this tier.
2. **Quality tier** (turn boundary; optional post-turn/async mode): digests, checkpoints, judge, escalation. Inline execution stays as the fallback when no turn boundary is available.

## Why it helps

- In-turn overflow recovery drops from minutes (worst case: tens of minutes) to seconds.
- Routine compaction stops stalling the agent (post-turn mode).
- Deterministic tool-result cleanup is the highest-value, lowest-risk compaction operation per published vendor evidence (+29–39% agent quality, −84% tokens — motivation, not a promise).

## Pros

- Both tiers reuse existing machinery: the deterministic hide and the local trim valve already exist — they are just bundled behind the judge today.

## Cons / risks

- Two paths must keep the same invariants (pair integrity, lossless hide, marker/ledger consistency).
- Post-turn mode changes UX timing; needs clear busy/status surfacing so "compacting between turns" is visible.
- keep-N-recent defaults need per-tool-class tuning.

## Acceptance

- TDD: the relief path completes deterministically with a dead/slow judge (no LM call attempted, bounded wall time); post-turn mode compacts between turns without inline stalls; invariants hold across tiers.
- >90% coverage; docs + CHANGELOG.

- **Session survival (owner directive):** every write this card adds is append-only/additive; no migration rewrites or replaces session files; a fixture proves an old (large) session loads unchanged — byte-identical apart from the new additive records.

Priority: **4 of 9** (auto-compact epic).

compaction.md
---
# Auto-compaction and the trigger tuning

Auto-compaction keeps a long session inside the model's context window by
folding older history into a structured checkpoint summary. This page is
about WHEN it fires — the trigger — and the `compaction:` config keys
that let you move it (gh-2098).

## The trigger model

The trigger evaluates TWO channels at every turn boundary and fires when
either crosses (gh-1742):

- **Estimate channel** — the chars/4 request estimate of the live
  transcript.
- **Observed channel** — the provider-reported accepted context of the
  last completed request (`usage.input + usage.cacheRead`). Observed
  wins: the pressure is `max(estimate, observed)`, and an
  observed-only crossing runs the pass FORCED (the estimate cannot see
  it).

Both channels compare against the same line: `window − reserveTokens`,
where the reserve comes from `CompactionSettings.forWindow(window)` —
the gh-1742 curve:

- `reserve = min(65536, max(window ~/ 16, legacy flat curve))` — 6.25%
  of the window on the proportional band (≥ 262,144), floored by the
  legacy flat 16Ki curve below it. Above 262k the trigger sits at
  **93.75% of the window**; on a 128k window the flat 16Ki reserve puts
  it at 87.2%.
- `keepRecentTokens = min(131072, max(window ~/ 8, legacy curve))` —
  where the context restarts after a pass.

## The tuning keys (gh-2098)

In `~/.fah/config.yaml` (user scope) or `<project>/.fah/config.yaml`
(project scope, wins per key):

```yaml
compaction:
  # Fire when the anchored context reaches 75% of the window.
```

  value, so EVERY window-derived consumer moves together: both trigger
  channels, the structured engine's gate and fragile-band escalation,
  the ctx meter, the spill budget, and subagent children (the CLI
  passes the merged section to the task executor).
- `reserveTokens` (positive int): the headroom set directly — the
  forWindow curve's reserve is replaced. `triggerRatio` and
  `reserveTokens` are two spellings of the same knob (the trigger
  line); configuring both is a boot error.
- `keepRecentTokens` (positive int): the post-compaction kept-recent
  region replaces the forWindow curve's.

**Absent keys → byte-identical gh-1742 behavior.** The tuning applies
over the scaled forWindow curve, not instead of it: a ratio overrides
only the trigger line, only a configured `keepRecentTokens` overrides
the keep curve.

Validation is strict (the whole `compaction:` section has been since
issue #148): a mistyped value, a ratio at/below 0 or at/above 1, a
non-positive budget, or the ratio+reserve combination throws a named
`ConfigException` at boot and at `fa config set` — nothing is persisted
that the next boot would reject.

Degenerate-guard note (mirrored from the forWindow curve): a reserve
over half the window (a ratio below ~0.5) clamps to `window ~/ 4`, and
a keep over the window clamps to `window ~/ 2` — a pass must always
free tokens.

Precedence for a run:

1. an explicit full `CompactionSettings` pin (hosts only — no yaml
   surface), with the tuning composed over it;
2. a non-empty `compaction:` tuning — a user pin;
3. the bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) over the forWindow
   curve — it retunes the DEFAULTS for a bench run and never rewrites a
   pinned section (gh-1604).

The Flutter app host does not read the tuning keys yet (it reads only
`compaction.engine` today — the same surface `judgeBudgetSeconds` had
before gh-2098); its wiring stays byte-identically on the forWindow
curve.

## Default decision and the benchmark note

**The legacy curve stays the default.** Absent keys are
byte-identical by contract; moving every session to the 0.75–0.80 band
silently multiplies compaction frequency (each pass is an LLM call on
the summarizer role — cost and latency), and the published Context Rot
curve degrades gracefully, not cliff-edge: the industry band buys
quality on very long sessions, at a measurable frequency price
everywhere. Operators of large-window classes opt in per scope; 0.80
is the informed middle (fires at 80% with a modest frequency increase).

Method (reproduce with your own recorded session — the curve is a
private artifact, the sim is standalone):

```bash
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <session.jsonl> \
  --window 128000 --window 200000 --window 400000
# deltas scaled ×3 = an emulated marathon riding the same per-request
# growth shape:
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <session.jsonl> --scale 3 \
  --window 200000 --window 400000
```

The sim replays the recorded per-request observed contexts
(`input + cacheRead`) as a sawtooth: on crossing the policy's line the
context restarts at the keep curve and continues riding the recorded
growth deltas.

cat >> docs/compaction.md << 'EOF'

## The two-tier engine (gh-209)

The engine splits by WHEN it may afford a language model:

### Emergency tier — mid-turn, deterministic, no LM

The loop's over-window guard and the message-cap self-heal (`gh-1680`)
call **only** the emergency tier (`EmergencyRelief`,
`lib/src/compaction/emergency_relief.dart`). It runs in seconds on any
path:

1. **Re-anchor** the live transcript from the session projection (the
   gh-2097 basis rule) and measure on the request-size basis.
2. **Dedup repeated reads** — for every read-class path seen more than
   once, the older pair groups fold into markers; the newest
   *successful* group stays live (its content is already on the wire).
   A group whose newest result failed never relieves its older
   successful copies.
3. **Keep-N-recent per tool class** — the newest N pair groups of each
   class stay live (read 2 / exec 4 / other 8, stalest-first folding of
   the rest) until the over-target amount is freed, net of the marker
   overhead.
4. **Local trim valve** — when the hides cannot free enough, the
   mechanical in-memory trim bounds the live context (the session file
   keeps every record).

No language model is attempted on ANY path — a dead or slow judge can
no longer turn an in-turn overflow into a long silent stall. The
invariants are the quality tier's: whole pair groups hide atomically
(pair integrity, #85/D6), real user turns and the protected tail and
pinned expansions never hide (F8/#1379), hides are lossless appends
(every id stays expandable behind its marker), and the relieved turn
continues visibly (`[resuming] continuing the turn on the compacted
context`).

### Quality tier — turn boundaries, judge-led

Digests, checkpoints, the judge and escalation run only at turn
boundaries (post-run and pre-flight), exactly as before. The over-window
funnel (issue #1085 M2) survives as the backstop: when the deterministic
tier cannot free the window (e.g. a keep-recent floor pinning the whole
transcript), the bounded classic/structured passes run and the exhaustion
verdict stays honest about how many ran.
EOF
echo done

A group whose newest result failed never relieves its older
   successful copies.
3. **Keep-N-recent per tool class** — the newest N pair groups of each
   class stay live (read 2 / exec 4 / other 8, stalest-first folding of
   the rest) until the over-target amount is freed, net of the marker
   overhead.
4. **Local trim valve** — when the hides cannot free enough, the

No language model is attempted on ANY path — a dead or slow judge can
no longer turn an in-turn overflow into a long silent stall. The
invariants are the quality tier's: whole pair groups hide atomically
(pair integrity, #85/D6), real user turns and the protected tail and
pinned expansions never hide (F8/#1379), hides are lossless appends
(every id stays expandable behind its marker), and the relieved turn
continues visibly (`[resuming] continuing the turn on the compacted
context`).

### Quality tier — turn boundaries, judge-led

Digests, checkpoints, the judge and escalation run only at turn
boundaries (post-run and pre-flight), exactly as before. The over-window
funnel (issue #1085 M2) survives as the backstop: when the deterministic
tier cannot free the window (e.g. a keep-recent floor pinning the whole
transcript), the bounded classic/structured passes run and the exhaustion
verdict stays honest about how many ran.

## Unreleased

- feat(gh-209): two-tier compaction engine — the mid-turn relief paths
  (the loop's over-window guard and the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal,
  CLI and Flutter app) now run ONLY the deterministic emergency tier
  (`EmergencyRelief`): re-anchor from the session projection, dedup
  repeated reads of the same path (the newest successful copy stays
  live), keep-N-recent per tool class stalest-first (read 2 / exec 4 /
  other 8 — `defaultEmergencyKeepRecent`), then the local trim valve.
  Seconds, bounded, ZERO language-model calls on any path — a dead or
  slow judge can no longer turn an in-turn overflow into the declared
  ≤15 min silent stall. All quality-tier invariants hold: whole pair
  groups hide atomically (#85/D6), real user turns / protected tail /
  pinned expansions never hide (F8/#1379), hides are lossless appends
  (every id stays expandable behind its marker), and the relieved turn
  continues visibly (`[resuming] …`). The quality tier (judge,
  checkpoints, escalation) stays at the turn boundaries — post-run and

  other 8 — `defaultEmergencyKeepRecent`), then the local trim valve —

  folds regardless of the class budgets (marker-reopenable; pinned
  expansions still veto).

arguments.content:
### What changed
- gh-209: mid-turn relief paths (the loop's over-window guard + the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal, CLI and Flutter app) now run ONLY the deterministic emergency tier (`EmergencyRelief`): re-anchor from the session projection, dedup repeated reads, keep-N-recent per tool class (read 2 / exec 4 / other 8), local trim valve — seconds, zero LM calls on any path. Quality tier (judge/checkpoints/escalation) stays at turn boundaries; the over-window funnel (#1085 M2) survives as backstop.
- New buster rule: a tool result that ALONE overflows the window folds regardless of class budgets/protected tail (marker-reopenable; pinned expansions still veto) — the app's IT-3 shape (single ~8.5k-token echo result) was unrecoverable without it.
- Flutter app `_relieveOverWindow` now mirrors the relieved transcript into the chat list (UI parity with the post-run compaction path).
- Test re-contracts to the deterministic face: `agent_cli_test` relief test (2 calls, no note/no records), E4 log-fidelity + fold-badge tests pin the relief decline and drive the funnel backstop (their gh-1433/#438 assertions unchanged); `agent_service_test` relief test pins `streamCalls == 2`.

### Key decisions
- Deliberate non-goal: the card's optional async post-turn compaction knob is NOT built — the emergency tier already removes the mid-turn LM stall; the quality tier owns boundaries.
- Buster floor keys on the WINDOW (refusal boundary), not the relief target — a result merely over the target still rides a valid request and belongs to the valve/keep-N passes.

### How to verify
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_over_window_continuation_retry_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_heal_test.dart test/cli/compaction_fold_badge_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_busy_gate_test.dart test/agent/` → 1284 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
- `cd flutter_app && touch .env && flutter test test/agent_service_compaction_it_test.dart test/agent_service_test.dart` → 77 passed (`.env` is a gitignored Flutter asset; CI creates the placeholder at job start).
- `dart analyze lib/src/cli lib/src/compaction` clean; `flutter analyze` errors are pre-existing `office_addin/dart/test/*` only.

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"neutral"}}%%
flowchart LR
    G[over-window guard / cap heal] --> E[EmergencyRelief: dedup → keep-N (+buster) → trim valve]
    E -- freed --> R[retry: '[resuming] continuing the turn']
    E -- declined --> F[funnel backstop: classic pass mid-turn]
    F -- freed --> R
    F -- exhausted --> X[honest exhaustion, no silent stall]
    B[turn boundary] --> Q[quality tier: judge / checkpoints / escalation]
```
